commits.message:
fix(effects): the close performs nothing, a repository answer lands with its click, and the tmux row is asked only when its switch moves (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.lhy)

- An effect the daemon's close cut off answers `closing`: the host performs
  no change or act once its close begins, a run the close aborted ends
  `closing`, and neither holds an error on any bar. A click's acts the close
  cut off answer its click `closing`, as its own steps do.
- A repository answer is performed only once its click's changes landed, and
  answered as they were otherwise, so the click lands whole.
- An act's failure joins a click error no answer has carried yet, at the
  input's instant, rather than replacing it.
- The tmux row is asked of the host only when a session's switch differs from
  the last ask. Once on, the host's adapter follows the session's pane at each
  request and forgets it when the session retires, so a request costs no act,
  no act line and no `effect-done` turn.
- Whatever types into a pane (a slash line, a lane setup) waits in one queue
  per pane.
- The act interpreter classifies a performer's throw, a synchronous one
  included; the act line is the one log of an outcome, and a reason names its
  act once.
- An act on a session reads it through a tagged result, not a structural guess.

feat(effects): every act a click or a lane switch causes is an effect the host performs (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.lhy)

The renderer no longer acts in place. A click's copy, open, slash line,
run, repository answer and update, and every lane setup, leave its turn as
a typed effect (`copy`, `open`, `type-slash`, `run`, `approve-repo`,
`apply-update`, `restart-claude`, `surface`). The host's act interpreter
performs each by kind and hands its outcome back as `effect-done`.

- One click path: a leaf link and a `dispatch` fold the same steps, and
  the per-verb wrappers are gone.
- The renderer's `Acts` ledger holds a failed act on its session's bar.
  One whose click named no session, or whose outcome reached no renderer,
  is the daemon's own `act-failed` warning on every bar.
- The host waits for the acts that end in a click's turn (copy, open,
  type-slash, approve-repo, apply-update), and the click is answered with
  how they ended. Runs, restarts and surfaces outlive it.
- Lane decisions (owed setups, the tmux row at each request) live in the
  renderer's `LaneSurfaces`. The host's `LaneSetups` only performs a
  surface or a restart, one at a time per session.
- The repository answer lands with the click's config changes, and its
  landing reloads the session's config before the click's lanes are
  measured, so an approved config that switches a lane on sets it up.
- The trust book's reader is shared and its writer is the host's.
- The adapter loses launch, typeSlash, applyUpdate, runs, laneSetups and
  tmuxStatusLines, and the hold-click-error push.
- The run owner's refusal count goes: a refused link is the click's bad
  request on its event line.

feat(click): a click's config writes are changes the host lands whole (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.axx) (#770)

* refactor(click): load-config and toolbar-toggle are deleted, so a session's config is only what its client named (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.axx)

* feat(click): a click's config writes are changes the host lands whole, so a refused one changes nothing (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.axx)

The renderer no longer writes a config file. A click's writes leave its
turn as `change` effects, one per file, each naming the settings it
touches and the JSON5 value it read there. The host performs a turn's
changes together or not at all, checking each setting against what was
read, so a hand edit elsewhere in the file never refuses a click and one
to the same setting always does.

What else a click did (the picks a save releases, its history step) is
its consequence: applied in the turn its changes land, after the clicking
session reloads, or dropped when they don't, with the reason on the ⚠.
A change refused because a setting moved also makes the session's history
forget that file; a write that fails for I/O keeps the step. A journal
turn opens only once the changes ahead of it have landed.

* fix(click): a refused click leaves nothing behind, and every click is answered after its landing (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.axx)

- Close no longer commits a click in flight: what a cut-off click wrote
  lands whole with its consequence, or not at all, so a refused click is
  never committed at shutdown.
- A refused click forgets only the files of the history steps it took; a
  landing names only the files its changes change.
- A landed click's reload and consequence each run, and any failure shows
  on the session's warning indicator.
- A second write to a file the click already wrote is applied over what
  the click wrote, and a contradiction is refused.
- The interpreter reads a file an earlier change removed as absent.
- The host answers a turn only after its effect-done turns, so a click is
  answered after its landing, in process or out of it.
- The renderer reads subscriptions as part of the turn, so a read that
  throws still hands on the turn's effects.

* fix(click): a click cut off by close lands nothing, and a history step lands all its files or none (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.axx)

- A click the daemon's close cut off seals nothing, so nothing of it is
  performed under the teardown.
- A step's file writes land together: one that contradicts the click
  lands none of them.
- The interpreter keys a turn's files by the file a write lands in, so
  two paths to one file are one rewrite.
- The host and the renderer read a config file through one reader.
- Edit mode's cancel memory line says what a moved file setting does.

* fix(history): a step's file is checked and proven at the click, so a hand edit is kept and named and no unloaded text is written (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.axx)

- Undo, redo and cancel write a file as the changes between the texts the
  step recorded, applied over the file as the click reads it. A setting
  that moved is stale there, like a moved session pick: named in the
  click's refusal, its file forgotten, and kept by cancel while everything
  else is put back.
- That text passes the loader gate every write passes before it lands,
  refused when the session no longer renders from the file.
- The refusal handler, the composition in the config writes, and the
  history's forget-a-file entry point are deleted: a host refusal now
  only meets a write that landed between the click's read and its landing.
- A refusal over a whole-file read no longer quotes the file twice.
- The spec's step 5 no longer schedules removing load-config.
